layer_title: Assumptions: costs, revenues and financing the pro-forma uses (dated, cited, refreshed)
note: Every figure here is an assumption, not a rule: the pro-forma is arithmetic over this layer and layer E. A figure with a public, machine-readable source is refreshed by `python -m ffm refresh`, which appends a new dated version; a figure read from a PDF carries a `verify` note and is typed by a person; a figure with no public source is marked `placeholder: true` in its source and the memo says so. Nothing here is invented silently.

rules.title: Hard construction cost, base ($/m², Vancouver)
rules.jurisdiction: BC Ministry of Housing / BC Housing (standardized designs)

params.summary: Hard cost base $4,693 per m² ($436 per build sq ft): the average of the three four-unit wood-frame designs in the Class D estimate for the Province's standardized housing designs, Vancouver baseline, August 2024, hard costs only
params.basis: average of Quadplex 01 ($425/sf), Quadplex 02 ($438/sf) and Townhouse ($446/sf); the catalogue's ten designs run $401 to $585 per build sq ft; the report's regional review gives Vancouver $350 to $475 per sq ft
params.excludes: soft costs, utility connections, existing buildings, rock or shoring, pad-mounted transformers (the report's stated assumptions)

source.title: SHP Class D Estimate Report, V3 (Chris Hill, CPA CMA, for the BC Ministry of Housing Standardized Designs Catalogue), 21 Aug 2024
source.section: Cost Estimate Summary (per build sf); Region Review; Assumptions
source.verify: The catalogue's designs are two- to four-unit, three-storey wood-frame buildings; a six-storey apartment sits outside it. Replace with a quantity surveyor's Class D figure for the actual building type when one exists, and keep this as the floor.

rules.title: Rents by tier: CMHC average market rent, rent-geared-to-income, the shelter rate
rules.jurisdiction: CMHC / BC Housing / Province of BC

params.summary: Market rent from the CMHC Rental Market Survey of October 2025, Vancouver CMA, purpose-built apartments: two-bedroom $2,363 a month, all unit types $1,963, vacancy 3.7% (the other bedroom types are left to be typed from the CMHC data tables); rent-geared-to-income at 30% of a household income taken, as a placeholder, at half the Community Housing Fund's low-to-moderate income limit for the unit size; the deep-subsidy rent at the income assistance shelter rate of $500

source.title: CMHC, Rental Market Report, January 2026 (October 2025 survey), Vancouver CMA; Province of BC, income assistance shelter allowance (single person, maximum $500 from 1 Dec 2025)
source.section: Vancouver: purpose-built rental vacancy 3.7%, average two-bedroom rent $2,363; summary by zone, all units $1,963
source.verify: Type the bachelor, one-bedroom and three-bedroom averages from the CMHC Rental Market Survey data tables (Vancouver CMA, Table 1.1.2); the rent-geared-to-income income placeholder is declared, not sourced: replace it with the operator's tenant income profile.

rules.title: Rent-geared-to-income and deep-subsidy rents, estimated the way BC Housing's call documents do

params.summary: Rent geared to income estimated at 30% of an income of 70% of the Housing Income Limit (Vancouver, in use from 1 Dec 2025: $58,000 for one bedroom or less, $72,000 for two, $86,000 for three): $1,015, $1,260 and $1,505 a month; deep-subsidy rent at the income assistance shelter allowance, $500 and $695, and for three bedrooms 30% of the deep-subsidy income limit, $769 a month
params.deep_subsidy_basis: one and two bedrooms: the income assistance shelter allowance for the household size, as the 2023 call printed it ($500, $695); three bedrooms and more: 30% of the 2026 deep-subsidy income limit for two bedrooms and more ($30,745)

source.title: BC Housing, Housing Income Limits (published October 2025, for use from 1 December 2025); Community Housing Fund request for proposals #1070-2324-041, Appendix 12 (RGI rent estimation tables)
source.section: HILs: Lower Mainland planning area, Vancouver row (the City of Vancouver is in the Vancouver HILs area, p.6). Appendix 12: rent-geared-to-income revenue on tenants averaging 70% of the Housing Income Limit; deep-subsidy revenue on the shelter allowance, and for three bedrooms and more on 30% of the deep-subsidy income limit
source.effective_from_basis: the day the Housing Income Limits read here came into use
source.verify: the 70% is the 2023 call's estimating assumption (the 2025 call's own appendix was not read) and an estimate, not a rent: replace it with the operator's tenant income profile; check the shelter allowances against the Province's current rates; a site outside the Vancouver HILs area needs its own row of the table
